reader.requirement: At --std 85 a NEXT GROUP clause (absolute, PLUS or NEXT PAGE) of a control footing that is processed at a level other than the highest level of the detected control break (at a GENERATE break, and at TERMINATE, whose highest level is FINAL when FINAL is a control, else the most major control) must have no effect, so the final LINE-COUNTER is the footing's last print line (§1985:XIII.3.10.8 GR6 a/b/c first paragraphs); the footing at the highest level applies its clause.

reader.notes: ProcessControlFootings walks the footings minor to the break level and passes applyNextGroup only for i == breakLevel; TERMINATE calls it with level 0 (FINAL when declared). An undeclared footing at the break level leaves every lower footing ignored, as the rule requires. All three NEXT GROUP forms probed at 85 behave as the 1985 table's GR6 first paragraphs say.

refuter.evidence: GENERATE-time breaks: the reader's ng3rel/ng3abs/ng3np agree with ProcessControlFootings (applyNextGroup only for i == breakLevel); not contested. TERMINATE is where the verdict rests on a reading. Probes E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-147/src/ngfin.cob (unpaged, CONTROLS ARE FINAL MAJ, NO CF FINAL declared, CF MAJ LINE PLUS 1 NEXT GROUP PLUS 3, RF LINE PLUS 1) and ngnof.cob (identical but CONTROLS ARE MAJ). --std 85: ngfin-001 'CFMAJ 07' then 'RFOOT 08', LC-AFTER 8; ngnof-001 'CFMAJ 07' then 'RFOOT 11', LC-AFTER 11. So writing the word FINAL in the CONTROL clause, with no FINAL group, silences the major footing's NEXT GROUP at TERMINATE (ProcessControlFootings(0), level 0 = the FINAL entry). The 1985 text: XIII.4.7.4 GR1 describes TERMINATE 'as though a control break has been sensed in the most major control data-name'; XIII.3.7.4 GR1 'FINAL, if specified, is the highest control, data-name-1 is the major control'; III.2 defines Control Data-Name as 'A data-name that appears in a CONTROL clause and refers to a control data item' (FINAL is not one; Control Break is 'A change in the value of a data item that is referenced in the CONTROL clause'). Read that way the highest level at which TERMINATE's break is sensed is data-name-1 (MAJ), so CF MAJ applies its NEXT GROUP in both programs (RFOOT on 11) and a CF FINAL, if declared, is the one ignored; the reader's ng3abs (CFMAJ PLUS 2 ignored at TERMINATE, CFFIN on 29) would then be wrong too (31 expected). The code's reading (FINAL is the break level because TERMINATE processes every footing) has no 1985 sentence of its own; the 'as though' clause is attached to the prior-values sentence, which leaves room for it. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.16.4 GR3  (3.16.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.4.7.4 GR1  (4.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.7.4 GR1  (3.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:III.2  (2. DEFINITIONS)  the text is in the clause'.
